translationRepairs: In the Wenyang campaign he met Zhu Xuan, Zhu Jin, and the Jin officer Shi Yan'er at the old Yue Pavilion and came back in triumph.
In the Wenyang campaign he fought Zhu Xuan, Zhu Jin, and the Jin officer Shi Yan'er at the old Yue Pavilion and came back in triumph.
戰 means that the forces fought a battle; 'met' understates the action.
The following year he joined Prince of Chen Zhu Youyu against Shi Pu at Dangshan, routed him, and took the foreign officer Shi Junhe and fifty more.
The following year he assisted the Prince of Chen, Zhu Youyu, against Shi Pu at Dangshan, routed him, and captured the foreign general Shi Junhe and fifty others.
The revision correctly separates Zhu Youyu's title and name and renders 佐 and 獲 directly.

Zhu Jin and Zan took fifty horsemen across the Huai by stealth, burst in from the north wall, and charged with levelled spears; the din rolled like thunder; Liang soldiers reeled and could not fight; Pang Cong was beheaded, senior officers fell in turn, and more than half the army was lost.)〉

Zhu Jin and Zan led fifty horsemen across the Huai by stealth, burst in from north of the camp, and charged while brandishing their lances; the din rolled like thunder; Liang soldiers reeled and could not fight; Pang Cong was beheaded, senior officers fell in turn, and more than half the army was lost.)〉
舞槊 means brandishing lances while charging. 壘北 is north of the camp, not a north wall.
Earlier Li Zhouyi had abandoned Yan and come over; he was made left marshal on the Founder's staff and stood first in favor at Bian.
Earlier Li Zhouyi had abandoned Fuzhou and come over; he was made left marshal on the Founder's staff and stood first in favor at the hegemonic headquarters.
鄜州 is Fuzhou, and 霸府 denotes the hegemonic headquarters rather than the city of Bian itself.
After the Founder took the throne he was given command; with Kang Huaaiying and others he besieged Luzhou behind the "Millipede Trench," so tight that no bird could cross.
After the Founder took the throne he was given command; with Kang Huaiying and others he besieged Luzhou behind the "Millipede Trench," so tight that no bird could cross.
康懷英 is Kang Huaiying; the existing Huaaiying is a typographical error.
When Qian's cause collapsed he fled to Yangzhou and attached himself to Ge Zuo.
When Qian's cause was about to collapse, he again fled to Yang Prefecture and attached himself to Ge Zuo.
洋州 is Yang Prefecture in the Hanzhong region. This wording distinguishes it from the better-known Yangzhou written 揚州.

In year 3 he was formally made commissioner of Yan-Fang, Special Advancement, and honorary Grand Guardian; he drilled the army and strengthened the walls until the people were secure, then was raised to honorary Grand Tutor.

In year 3 he was formally made commissioner of Fu-Fang, Special Advancement, and honorary Grand Guardian; he drilled the army and strengthened the walls until the people were secure, then was raised to honorary Grand Tutor.
鄜坊 is the Fu-Fang circuit, not Yan-Fang.
In Qianhua 2, after Yougui seized the throne, Zhu Youqian of Hezhong rebelled, stormed Yanzhou, and took Huaiyu unawares; he was held prisoner in the official residence.
In Qianhua 2, after Yougui seized the throne, Zhu Youqian of Hezhong rebelled, stormed Fuzhou, and took Huaiyu unawares; he was held prisoner in the official residence.
The attacked prefecture is 鄜州, Fuzhou, not Yanzhou.
The Founder rewarded him with the title "Array-Slashing Champion" and soon had him made prefect of Xu and honorary Right Vice Director.
The Founder rewarded him with the title "Array-Slashing Champion" and soon had him made prefect of Suzhou and honorary Right Vice Director.
宿州 is Suzhou, not Xuzhou. The Chinese characters are unnecessary in the running English text.
In the second month of Zhonghe 4, when Shang Rang raided Fantai, Tangbin served Chao with Li Zan and Huo Cun and fought the Founder outside the Weishi Gate.
In the second month of Zhonghe 4, when Shang Rang raided Fantai, Tangbin served Chao with Li Dang and Huo Cun and fought the Founder outside the Weishi Gate.
李讜 is Li Dang. The parenthetical Chinese is not needed once the name is corrected.
In Guangming of Tang, when Huang Chao marched west into Qin and Yong, Yan was impressed into his ranks.
In Guangming of Tang, when Huang Chao marched west into Qin and Yong, Yan was seized by Chao's partisans.
為巢黨所執 states that Yan was seized by Huang Chao's partisans; 'impressed into his ranks' adds an unstated result.
Months later the Jin returned; the Founder's main force was fighting Yan and Yan and could not relieve the city.
Months later the Jin returned; the Founder's main force was fighting Yan and Yun and could not relieve the city.
兗 and 鄆 are the distinct prefectures Yan and Yun. The repeated Yan is a translation error.
In the long wars on Xu, Yan, and Yan he was usually victorious and excelled at entrenchments, serving as trench commissioner for all forces.
In the long wars on Xu, Yan, and Yun he was usually victorious and excelled at entrenchments, serving as trench commissioner for all forces.
The same 兗、鄆 pair must read Yan and Yun here as well.
In year 2, after Yougui seized the throne, he was made honorary Minister of War.
In year 2, after Yougui seized the throne, he was made honorary Minister over the Masses.
司徒 is Minister over the Masses. Minister of Works is 司空, while Minister of War is not the office named here.
In the first month of year 7 he took command of Hua.
In the first month of year 7 he took command of Huazhou.
滑州 is Huazhou; spelling out the prefecture name removes the ambiguity without a parenthetical gloss.
The Prince of Jin marched east from Huangze Ridge to Linqing; Delun sent Sikong Yan secretly to tell him of Zhang Yan's abuse.
The Prince of Jin marched east from Huangze Ridge to Linqing; Delun sent Sikong Ting secretly to tell him of Zhang Yan's abuse.
司空頲 is Sikong Ting. The source characters need not be inserted into the running translation.
Autumn, month 9, the court learned the Jin army would march from Yanzhou; the Last Emperor sent Yanzhang with several thousand Palace Guard cavalry to hold the east.

In autumn, the ninth month, the court learned the Jin army would march via the Yanzhou road; the Last Emperor urgently sent Yanzhang with several thousand Baoluan Palace Guard cavalry to hold the eastern route.
The proposal restores the urgency, the Yanzhou route, and the specific Baoluan cavalry guard named in the source.
